gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-krub: Heavy, stubborn, a little wiry: Plakkaat bends its lines like straw and curls its terminals nearly shut. Krub answers that tightness with tall lowercase and curves left deliberately unfinished, so the loops stay open.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-lexend:
Lexend reads wide and friendly, with oversized lowercase and open curves.

Plakkaat's bold, closed, nearly touching terminals make a sharp partner, since the heavy display letters and the open sans below trade tightness for breathing room.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-lexend-deca: Plakkaat brings heavy, wiry letters whose terminals curl almost back to the stem. Lexend Deca stays plain and unshaded beneath it, with small capitals beside big lowercase, so the heading can be given extra size.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-mada:
Plakkaat's lines look like bent straw, uniform on every letter.

Mada, a sans with towering midzone letters and curves that refuse to close, would carry a long passage in an easygoing, modern way without competing with that heavy heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-nobile:
Professional in tone, Nobile is a sans-serif with chalk-arc letter mouths and capitals sitting barely above its lowercase, set against Plakkaat's heavy, nearly closed forms.

Closed against open is the pair's whole story.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-kufi-arabic:
Noto Kufi Arabic opens with a welcoming gap in the c and capitals barely above lowercase, a modern, clean sans.

Noto Kufi Arabic's openness against Plakkaat's wire-cut, heavy strokes is the strongest quality here: dense, uniform display letters over generous, airy ones.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam:
Dense and heavy up top, wide open below.

Noto Sans Adlam, a sans-serif with curve endings kept well apart and tall, full c, s and z, would read smoothly and openly beneath Plakkaat's nearly closed, bent-straw heading letters.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam-u:
Wire-cut letters, heavy and tight.

Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined, a professional sans-serif with generous gaps where curves meet the stem, makes the strongest contrast: Plakkaat closes its terminals while this body leaves them open.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-anatoli:
Modern, yet heavy at heart.

Plakkaat is best at bold, bent-straw display lines with terminals curling shut, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, a sans-serif, does its best work with outward-pointing tips and an x-height rising near cap height.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-avestan:
Modern and clean below, heavy and tightly curled above.

The strongest quality is closed against open: Plakkaat's terminals nearly touch the stem, while Noto Sans Avestan, a plain sans, keeps its curve tips apart with a pronounced x-height.
